---
title: "Analysis, code or files do not work"
last-reviewed: "2026-09-08"
---

## Preserve the evidence first

Save the error message and the command that produced it before changing anything. Note the input files, code version, software environment, what you expected and what happened. Keep the last working version if you have it.

## Try this now

1. Reproduce the failure only if repeating the action is safe.
2. Reduce it to a small example that contains no protected data.
3. Check where it begins: the inputs, software, settings, code logic, saved session state, dependencies, available resources or output step.
4. Change one thing and record what happened.
5. Once it works, rerun from the original approved inputs in a fresh session and check the important outputs.

If another run could delete files, overwrite the only copy, expose data or incur a charge, preserve the evidence you already have and seek help first. For an ordinary code error, a few invented rows may be enough to demonstrate it. For a formatting problem, try a copy containing only the affected table or paragraph.

## What to take when asking

Share the steps, full error, safe example data, software details and fixes you've tried. Remove credentials and protected data before asking online.

## Stop or escalate

Contact the appropriate research or IT service for possible data loss, a security incident or a permission problem. Tell your supervisor if reported results can't be reproduced. Bypassing access controls is not a repair.

## You are moving again when

The work runs from a fresh session, you've checked its outputs and another authorised person can follow the same steps.

Use [Technical failure](../chapters/part-11/32-technical-failure-perfectionism.qmd) and the [before-analysis checklist](../checklists/before-analysis.qmd).
